digest.component_or_area: policy gate: shrink-only ratchet for git mutations
propositions: The existing git-write checker (R1/R2, policy d37e) enforces mechanism (no raw subprocess git) but not protocol (mutations must go through atomic transaction), permitting composed git_adapter primitives outside the reconciler write seam.

Rule R3 fires when a git-adapter mutation primitive (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) is called from outside the sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), resolved by receiver binding (import or dynamic-loader).

R3 binds on RECEIVER NAME (git_adapter module reference), not bare attribute, so set.add() and session.commit() do not fire; sanctioned entries are the seam files themselves, where primitives are defined and composed under the ref lock.

Two out-of-transaction sites take durable reasoned inline markers: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) due to selective staging boundary, and __main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks) via detached temp index with CAS ref-advance (concurrency-safe).

R3 is added to the existing checker (one gate, one marker vocabulary, one CI wiring), with unit tests covering false-positive floor (set.add, session.commit, read-only exports), seam-internal exemption, and marker semantics (reasoned vs. reasonless).

File split extracted pass-lock lifecycle (_lock_steal_enabled, _resolve_held_lock, _purge_committed_reconciler_locks, _acquire_or_adopt_pass_lock) from __main__.py to _pass_lock_lifecycle.py to satisfy module-size gate; seam-composition markers travelled with relocated function.
